executiveDecision: Ineligible / Review Required due to protocol laboratory threshold deviations and incomplete exclusion washout documentation.
executiveSummary: Participant PT-1042 fails multiple protocol-defined screening laboratory criteria (Hemoglobin, ANC, Platelets, Creatinine, ALT, and AST). Additionally, unconfirmed prednisone washout, an out-of-window Day 15 visit deviation (conducted on Day 21), ongoing Grade 2 nausea/vomiting AE, and missing affirmative documentation for non-laboratory exclusion criteria preclude immediate clearance without further clinical review and protocol deviation/eligibility reconciliation.

priorityFindings.title: Multiple Screening Laboratory Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria Violations
priorityFindings.finding: Participant lab values fail protocol screening thresholds across 6 parameters: Hemoglobin (10.2 g/dL vs >=12.0 g/dL required), ANC (1.1 ×10⁹/L vs >=1.5 ×10⁹/L required), Platelets (145 ×10⁹/L vs >=150 ×10⁹/L required), Creatinine (1.4 mg/dL vs <=1.2 mg/dL required), ALT (82 U/L vs <=45 U/L required), and AST (76 U/L vs <=40 U/L required).
priorityFindings.whyItMatters: Failing screening laboratory thresholds impacts participant eligibility, participant safety during investigational dosing, and protocol compliance.
priorityFindings.interpretation: Participant PT-1042 does not meet baseline laboratory eligibility criteria specified in the study protocol.

evidence.fact: Hemoglobin screening threshold: >=12.0 g/dL; ANC screening threshold: >=1.5 ×10⁹/L; Platelet screening threshold: >=150 ×10⁹/L; Creatinine screening threshold: <=1.2 mg/dL; ALT screening threshold: <=45 U/L; AST screening threshold: <=40 U/L.
Hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL, ANC 1.1 ×10⁹/L, Platelets 145 ×10⁹/L, Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL, ALT 82 U/L, AST 76 U/L.

missingEvidence: Repeat laboratory assessments or protocol waiver documentation.
priorityFindings.recommendedAction: Verify whether re-screening/repeat testing is permitted under protocol or log an eligibility protocol deviation.

priorityFindings.title: Unconfirmed Steroid Washout and Missing Non-Laboratory Inclusion Evidence
priorityFindings.finding: Prednisone exposure ended on 05-Aug-2026, but the dose, route, and required protocol washout period are undocumented. Additionally, several non-laboratory eligibility criteria lack affirmative source evidence.
priorityFindings.whyItMatters: Unverified steroid washout or unconfirmed exclusion areas (e.g., uncontrolled infection, cardiovascular disease) present compliance risks and potential participant safety hazards.
priorityFindings.interpretation: Without exact prednisone dose and protocol washout specifications, prohibited medication exclusion compliance cannot be confirmed.

evidence.fact: Prohibited medication and washout requirements must be confirmed against the active protocol. Uncontrolled infection, recent major surgery, prohibited concomitant medication, and clinically significant cardiovascular disease are listed exclusion areas.

Recent prednisone exposure ended 05-Aug-2026; dose and protocol washout applicability are not documented. The participant summary states that several non-laboratory criteria lack affirmative source evidence.
Prednisone was documented from 01-Aug-2026 through 05-Aug-2026. Prednisone dose, route and full protocol restriction context are not documented.

missingEvidence: Affirmative source documentation for non-laboratory exclusion criteria.
priorityFindings.recommendedAction: Obtain prednisone administration log (dose/route) and complete the non-laboratory eligibility checklist.

priorityFindings.title: Ongoing Grade 2 Nausea/Vomiting Post-Treatment
priorityFindings.finding: Grade 2 nausea with intermittent vomiting began 05-Aug-2026, approximately 18 hours after study treatment, leading to a temporary dose hold and oral antiemetic initiation.
priorityFindings.whyItMatters: Determines dose modification, safety reporting, and treatment continuation suitability.
priorityFindings.interpretation: Event is temporally associated with study treatment administration and preliminarily assessed as possibly related, but expectedness and final causality remain incomplete.

evidence.fact: Grade 2 nausea with intermittent vomiting began 05-Aug-2026 approximately 18 hours after study treatment. Study dose was temporarily held and oral antiemetic therapy was initiated. Preliminary investigator causality was possibly related.

priorityFindings.recommendedAction: Obtain updated AE follow-up details, expectedness assessment, and confirmation of whether study dose resume criteria are met.

priorityFindings.title: Protocol Deviation: Out-of-Window Day 15 Visit and Delayed CBC
priorityFindings.finding: The Day 15 visit window was Day 13 through Day 17, but the visit and CBC collection occurred on Day 21 due to transportation issues.
priorityFindings.whyItMatters: Out-of-window lab collection delays safety evaluation of hematologic parameters and constitutes a protocol deviation.
priorityFindings.interpretation: Late collection creates a data gap regarding hematologic status during the intended Day 13-17 safety window.

evidence.fact: Day 15 visit window was Day 13 through Day 17; actual visit occurred Day 21. CBC was collected on Day 21 rather than within the Day 15 visit window. Transportation issues are documented as the reason.

missingEvidence: Investigator assessment of deviation severity and impact on participant safety/data integrity.
priorityFindings.recommendedAction: Complete protocol deviation log with formal investigator impact assessment.
